title: Rank-one local calculation
statement:
In the finite-torsion setting of [def-pur-conventions], let $A=A_{E,n}$ for any $n\geq1$, and choose an integer $N\geq1$ such that $\ell^N A=0$. Let $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ be a geometric point of a $k$-scheme, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed, and put
$$
X=\mathbf A^1_\Omega=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega[t],\qquad
Z=V(t)\subset X,\qquad U=X\setminus Z=\mathbf G_{m,\Omega}.
$$
Thus $Z$ is the fibre of the zero section of $\mathbf A^1_Y\to Y$. On the small etale site set
$$
A(1)=\mu_{\ell^N}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^N}\underline A.
$$
Use cohomology with supports as in [def-pur-support-cohomology]. Let $\delta_N$ be the boundary of the Kummer sequence [def-sc-kummer-sequence], and let $\kappa_A(u)\in H^1(U,A(1))$ be the image of $\delta_N(u)$ under the coefficient map $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Then the support boundary of [thm-pur-with-support-exactness] is an isomorphism
$$
\partial:H^1(U,A(1))\xrightarrow{\sim}H^2_Z(X,A(1)),
$$
and there is a unique $A$-linear isomorphism
$$
\rho:H^2_Z(X,A(1))\xrightarrow{\sim}A,\qquad
\rho\bigl(\partial\kappa_A(t)\bigr)=1.
$$
In particular $H^q_Z(X,A(1))=0$ for every $q\geq0$ with $q\neq2$. The composite $\rho\partial$ is the residue homomorphism: for every global unit $u=c t^r$ on $U$, with $c\in\Omega^\times$ and $r\in\mathbf Z$,
$$
\rho\bigl(\partial\kappa_A(u)\bigr)=r\cdot1_A=\operatorname{ord}_0(u)\cdot1_A.
$$
Here $\operatorname{ord}_0$ is the exponent of $t$ in a nonzero rational function at $0$, so $t$ has order $1$ and every unit of $\Omega[t]_{(t)}$ has order $0$. The normalization is independent of a primitive root of unity; such a choice, provided by [lem-sc-primitive-root] and [def-sc-mu-trivialization], is used only to identify the degree-zero groups with $A$. The same result holds on the small pro-etale site for the inverse-image coefficient sheaf, under [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison].

external.place: Source: Milne, Lectures on Etale Cohomology, Section 14, Proposition 14.3, and Example 16.3.) Write $X=\mathbf A^1_{\bar y}$, $U=\mathbf G_{m,\bar y}$, and apply the long exact sequence for cohomology with support [thm-pur-with-support-exactness] to the pair $(X,Z)$: $$ \begin{array}{l} 0\to H^0_Z(X,A(1))\to H^0(X,A(1))\to H^0(U,A(1))\to H^1_Z(X,A(1))\\ \hphantom{0\to{}} \to H^1(X,A(1))\to H^1(U,A

proof.text: Put $m=\ell^N$ and $R=\mathbf Z/m$. Since $\ell\neq\operatorname{char}\Omega$, [lem-sc-primitive-root] supplies a primitive $m$-th root $\zeta$. By [def-sc-mu-trivialization], $\mu_m$ on $X$ and $U$ is the constant free rank-one $R$-sheaf. For every finite $R$-module $M$ write $M(1)=\mu_m\otimes_R\underline M$; this is therefore isomorphic to $\underline M$ on each curve. Both curves are nonempty and connected: their coordinate rings $\Omega[t]$ and $\Omega[t,t^{-1}]$ are domains, and the zero prime belongs to every nonempty principal open, so two nonempty opens cannot be disjoint. The statement [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-connected] now identifies $H^0(X,M(1))$ and $H^0(U,M(1))$ with $M$, using this same $\zeta$. Restriction is the identity because it restricts the constant section labelled by $a\in M$ to the section with the same label. These identifications are natural in $M$.

source.place: Imported proof paragraph 1: the identical H^0 identifications and their restriction map

proof.text:
We extend the free-coefficient computation to all finite $R$-modules, without imposing freeness on $A$. Define
$$
\tau_M:M\longrightarrow H^1(U,M(1)),\qquad a\longmapsto H^1(x\mapsto x\otimes a)(\delta_N(t)).
$$
This map is additive and natural in $M$: for $f:M\to M'$, the coefficient maps satisfy $(1\otimes f)(x\otimes a)=x\otimes f(a)$, and cohomology preserves their sums and composites. It is also $R$-linear: for $r\in R$, the coefficient map $i_{ra}:x\mapsto x\otimes ra$ equals multiplication by $r$ composed with $i_a$, so $\tau_M(ra)=r\tau_M(a)$. We prove by induction on $|M|$ that $H^{q>0}(X,M(1))=0$, $H^{q\geq2}(U,M(1))=0$, and $\tau_M$ is an isomorphism. For $M=0$ these claims are immediate. For $M=\mathbf F_\ell$, [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], with levels $\ell\mid\ell^N$, identifies $\mu_{\ell^N}\otimes_R\mathbf F_\ell$ with $\mu_\ell$. It carries $\delta_N(t)$ to $\delta_1(t)$: the diagram of the two exact Kummer sequences [lem-sc-kummer-exact] uses $z\mapsto z^{\ell^{N-1}}$ on the first $\mathbf G_m$ and the identity on the second, so the powers commute. Equivalently, local roots $v_i^{\ell^N}=t$ give roots $v_i^{\ell^{N-1}}$ of $t$ of order $\ell$, with transition ratios raised to $\ell^{N-1}$. Use the $\mathcal V$-small skeleton of each site fixed by [def-weil-size-convention], so the site-size hypothesis below holds. Abelian sheaves on this site have enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives]. The natural connecting maps of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor] give the asserted equality of classes. Apply [thm-pur-kummer-affine-line] at exponent one and coefficient ring $\mathbf F_\ell$, which is free of rank one over itself. This proves precisely the induction claims for $\mathbf F_\ell$.

source.place: Unit proof, Coefficients and Degrees 0 and 1: prime-coefficient base of the coefficient devissage needed in imported proof paragraph 1

proof.text:
For a nonzero finite $R$-module $M$ not isomorphic to the base module $\mathbf F_\ell$, choose $a\neq0$ and the least $r\geq1$ with $\ell^r a=0$. Then $b=\ell^{r-1}a$ has order $\ell$, so its cyclic submodule $C=Rb$ is isomorphic to $\mathbf F_\ell$. Put $Q=M/C$; both $|C|$ and $|Q|$ are smaller than $|M|$. The base computation applies to $C$ through the isomorphism $\mathbf F_\ell\to C$, $1\mapsto b$, and the naturality of $\tau$; thus the induction is on modules up to isomorphism. The sequence $0\to\underline C\to\underline M\to\underline Q\to0$ is exact: it is the sheafification of the objectwise exact sequence of constant presheaves, and [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact] states that sheafification is exact. Tensoring with $\mu_m$ preserves this sequence because the trivialization of step 1 identifies that tensor functor with the identity. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-cohomology-long-exact-ladder] with the identity scheme map on each of $X,U$, to obtain the coefficient long exact sequences. The induction hypotheses for $C,Q$ imply all the required higher vanishings for $M$: the relevant cohomology group is between the zero groups for $C,Q$. On $U$, the degree-zero map $M\to Q$ is surjective by step 1, and $H^2(U,C(1))=0$, so the same sequence gives
$$
0\to H^1(U,C(1))\to H^1(U,M(1))\to H^1(U,Q(1))\to0.
$$
Naturality of $\tau$ puts this under $0\to C\to M\to Q\to0$. The outside vertical maps are isomorphisms. Explicitly, to lift a middle cohomology class, lift its $Q$-label to $M$ and subtract its $\tau_M$-image; the remainder comes from $H^1(U,C(1))$ and hence from $C$. If $\tau_M(a)=0$, its $Q$-label is zero, so $a$ comes from $C$; injectivity of the left cohomology arrow and of $\tau_C$ gives $a=0$. Thus $\tau_M$ is an isomorphism, completing the induction. In particular it applies to $M=A$ for every $n$. For $A$, $\tau_A(a)=a\kappa_A(t)$, so this is an $A$-linear isomorphism.

source.place: Unit proof, Coefficients: full induction step, retaining arbitrary n rather than the free-coefficient restriction of thm-pur-kummer-affine-line

proof.text:
Apply [thm-pur-with-support-exactness] to the closed origin $Z\subset X$ and the torsion sheaf $A(1)$. Substituting steps 1--3 gives
$$
0\to H^0_Z(X,A(1))\to A\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}A\to H^1_Z(X,A(1))\to0\to A\xrightarrow{\partial\tau_A}H^2_Z(X,A(1))\to0.
$$
Hence $H^0_Z=H^1_Z=0$ and $\partial\tau_A$ is an isomorphism. For $q\geq3$, exactness puts $H^q_Z$ between $H^{q-1}(U,A(1))=0$ and $H^q(X,A(1))=0$, so it vanishes too. Functoriality of the support sequence in $F$ makes $\partial$ commute with multiplication by every $a\in A$; hence $\partial$ and $\partial\tau_A$ are $A$-linear. Define $\rho=(\partial\tau_A)^{-1}$, an $A$-linear isomorphism. This proves all asserted groups and the normalization $\rho(\partial\kappa_A(t))=1$.

source.place: Imported proof paragraph 1: support long exact sequence; paragraph 2: all vanishing groups and normalized degree-two isomorphism

proof.text: By [lem-pur-affine-punctured-line-algebra], every global unit of $U$ is $c t^r$, with $c\in\Omega^\times$ and $r\in\mathbf Z$. The Kummer boundary from the exact sequence [lem-sc-kummer-exact] is a group homomorphism. Since $\Omega$ is algebraically closed, $c$ has an $m$-th root, so its boundary is zero; therefore $\kappa_A(c t^r)=r\kappa_A(t)$. Applying $\rho\partial$ gives $r\cdot1_A$. For a polynomial, factor out the highest power of $t$; for a quotient of polynomials subtract these exponents. This defines $\operatorname{ord}_0$ on $\Omega(t)^\times$. A unit in $\Omega[t]_{(t)}$ has numerator and denominator both nonzero at zero, hence order zero, while $\operatorname{ord}_0(t)=1$. In particular $\operatorname{ord}_0(c t^r)=r$, proving the claimed residue formula with its sign fixed by $t$.

source.place: Imported proof paragraph 2: replace the erroneous unit/completed-local-ring/orbit sentence by the explicit valuation normalization

proof.text: The map $\partial\tau_A$ is defined using only the specified support boundary and the coefficient image of the Kummer class of $t$; neither definition uses $\zeta$. Thus its inverse $\rho$ is independent of the primitive root used to compute the degree-zero groups. Since $\partial\kappa_A(t)$ is an $A$-basis, any $A$-linear map taking it to $1$ must equal $\rho$, proving uniqueness and canonicity. The freeness in this argument is the conclusion that $H^1(U,A(1))$ is free of rank one over $A$; no freeness of $A$ over $R$ has been assumed.

source.place: Imported proof paragraph 2: canonicity of the normalized isomorphism

proof.text:
Put $F=A(1)$ and $F_p=\nu_X^*F$. Apply [lem-pur-support-comparison-boundary] to $(T,C)=(X,Z)$ over the algebraically closed field $\Omega$: $X=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega[t]$ is separated and finite type over $\Omega$, $Z=V(t)$ is closed, and $A$ is a finite commutative ring. Thus the lemma applies even when $\Omega$ is not finite type over the fixed field $k$. The coefficient sheaf is the ordinary finite discrete $A$-module sheaf, in degree zero. Write $c_U$ for its ordinary degree-one comparison and $c_Z$ for its supported degree-two comparison. These are isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology] and [lem-pur-support-site-comparison], respectively. The boundary compatibility supplied by the new lemma is
$$c_Z\partial_{\mathrm{et}}=\partial_{\mathrm{pro}}c_U.$$
The same comparisons in every degree transfer the ordinary and supported vanishings of steps 1--4 to the pro-etale site, and transfer the degree-zero restriction map as well.

source.place: Final sentence: transport to the pro-etale site, retaining the actual support boundary and its Kummer normalization

proof.text:
All maps in the boundary square of step 7 are $A$-linear by [lem-pur-support-comparison-boundary]. Solving that square, using the invertible maps already established, gives
$$\partial_{\mathrm{pro}}=c_Z\partial_{\mathrm{et}}c_U^{-1},\qquad c_Z=\partial_{\mathrm{pro}}c_U\partial_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}.$$
Set $\tau_{\mathrm{pro}}=c_U\tau_A$ and $\rho_{\mathrm{pro}}=(\partial_{\mathrm{pro}}\tau_{\mathrm{pro}})^{-1}$. Then
$$\rho_{\mathrm{pro}}c_Z=(\partial_{\mathrm{et}}\tau_A)^{-1}=\rho.$$
This is the original conjugation construction of the supported comparison, now identified with its canonical comparison map.

source.place: Final sentence: transport to the pro-etale site, retaining the actual support boundary and its Kummer normalization

proof.text:
The inverse-image coefficient class on the pro-etale site is $c_U\kappa_A(u)$. Hence the square and the inverse identity in steps 7--8 give
$$\rho_{\mathrm{pro}}\partial_{\mathrm{pro}}c_U\kappa_A(u)=\rho\partial_{\mathrm{et}}\kappa_A(u)=r\cdot1_A\quad(u=ct^r).$$
For $u=t$ this value is $1$. The element $c_U\kappa_A(t)$ is an $A$-basis since $c_U\tau_A$ is an isomorphism, so its boundary determines $\rho_{\mathrm{pro}}$ uniquely. The definitions use no primitive root, and the vanishing in every other supported degree was transferred in step 7. This proves all the pro-etale assertions.

source.place: Final sentence: transport to the pro-etale site, retaining the actual support boundary and its Kummer normalization

blueprint_update.statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
$A=A_{E,n}$, let $\bar y\to Y$ be a
geometric point of $Y$ with
algebraically closed field $\Omega$, put
$Z=s(\bar y)\subset\mathbf A^1_{\bar y}=\mathbf A^1_k\times_k\Omega$, and
let $A(1)$ be the finite-level twist
$A(1)=\mu_{\ell^N}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^N}A$ on the
smooth separated curve $\mathbf A^1_{\bar y}$
over $\Omega$. Then there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
H^2_Z\bigl(\mathbf A^1_{\bar y},A(1)\bigr)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }A,
$$

under which the boundary of the
Kummer class of the coordinate $t$
corresponds to $1\in A$; equivalently, the boundary map of the
support long exact sequence

$$
\partial:\ H^1\bigl(\mathbf G_{m,\bar y},A(1)\bigr)
\longrightarrow H^2_Z\bigl(\mathbf A^1_{\bar y},A(1)\bigr)
$$

is the *residue* homomorphism and its value on $\kappa(t)$ is
the residue $1$, given by the normalization
$\operatorname{ord}_0(t)=1$ (the order of a unit of the completed
local ring at the origin is the exponent of $t$, so the boundary
of the Kummer class of the coordinate is the class of the orbit
$t\cdot(\mathbf G_m^\wedge)^{(N)}$); all other supported cohomology
groups of $A(1)$ vanish:

$$
H^q_Z(\mathbf A^1_{\bar y},A(1))=0\qquad(q\neq2).
$$

The statements are those of the etale site, transported to the pro-etale
site by [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], the coefficients being
finite-torsion. (The identification of the $H^0$-terms and of
$A(1)_{\bar y}\cong A$ uses a primitive $\ell^N$-th root of unity in
$\Omega$, in the sense of [def-sc-mu-trivialization], and
[lem-sc-primitive-root] for its existence.)

proof.text:
Write $X=\mathbf A^1_{\bar y}$, $U=\mathbf G_{m,\bar y}$, and apply
the long exact sequence for cohomology with support
[thm-pur-with-support-exactness] to the pair $(X,Z)$:

$$
\begin{array}{l}
0\to H^0_Z(X,A(1))\to H^0(X,A(1))\to H^0(U,A(1))\to H^1_Z(X,A(1))\\
\hphantom{0\to{}}
\to H^1(X,A(1))\to H^1(U,A(1))\to H^2_Z(X,A(1))\to H^2(X,A(1))\\
\hphantom{0\to{}}
\to H^2(U,A(1))\to H^3_Z(X,A(1))\to H^3(X,A(1))\to\cdots.
\end{array}
$$

By [thm-pur-kummer-affine-line] (with the field $\Omega$),
$H^q(X,A(1))=0$ for $q>0$,
$H^0(X,A(1))=H^0(U,A(1))=A$, and the groups on $U$ vanish except
$H^1(U,A(1))=A$, generated by the Kummer class of $t$. The
restriction map $H^0(X,A(1))\to H^0(U,A(1))$ is the identity under the
identical identification of both groups with $A$ (the sheaf $A(1)$ is
locally constant, i.e. constant after the trivialization of
[def-sc-mu-trivialization], and both schemes are connected), so the
sequence reads

$$
0\to H^0_Z(X,A(1))\to A\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }A\to H^1_Z(X,A(1))\to
0\to A\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^2_Z(X,A(1))\to 0\to 0\to\cdots.
$$

Exactness gives $H^0_Z=0$, $H^1_Z=0$, and

$$
H^2_Z(X,A(1))\cong A,
$$

the isomorphism sending the boundary of the Kummer class of $t$ to the
generator $1\in A$. Explicitly, the boundary of the support sequence is
the residue map, and its value on the Kummer class is the valuation at
the origin: under the identification
$H^1(U,A(1))\cong A$ generated by $\kappa(t)$ and
$H^2_Z(X,A(1))\cong A$, the isomorphism of the statement is
$\kappa(t)\mapsto\operatorname{ord}_0(t)=1$, i.e. the exponential of
the valuation of the completing local ring
$\mathcal O_{X,Z}^{\wedge}\cong\Omega[[t]]$, whose unit
$t$ has order one. The displayed identifications fix the
normalization without a choice of splitting (the classes of the
coordinate torsor and its boundary are the same as the classes of the
global coordinate, by the torsor form of the Kummer class of
[def-pur-affine-line-datum]). The groups $H^q_Z$ vanish for
$q>2$ since they
sit between the vanishing $H^{q-1}(U,A(1))$ and $H^q(X,A(1))$. The
pro-etale form is the comparison [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] of
the proper-base-change chapter.
